practices.practice: Require TLS in the connection string (e.g., tls=true) and use the mongodb+srv scheme with SCRAM-SHA-256 authentication when connecting to an Azure DocumentDB cluster.

practices.practice: Create explicit indexes that match your app's filter and sort patterns (single-field and compound indexes for claimId/transactionId/createdAt etc.) and verify queries use them with explain().
practices.prior_belief: Create explicit indexes for filter and sort patterns used by the app — e.g., an index on { claimId: 1 }, a compound index on { transactionId: 1, timestamp: -1 }, and an index on decision status + updatedAt — and verify with explain() that queries use those indexes.

practices.practice: Run explain('executionStats') and use $indexStats to inspect execution plans, measure totalDocsExamined/totalKeysExamined, and confirm index selection before changing indexes.

practices.practice: Avoid adding every possible index up front; iterate indexes using explain() / Index Advisor to prevent unnecessary write amplification.

practices.practice: Use TTL indexes for ephemeral records (logs, temp evidence caches) so documents expire automatically instead of accumulating indefinitely.

practices.practice: Keep individual documents under the BSON document size limit (16 MB) and store large attachments (PDFs, images) outside DocumentDB (Blob storage) with references in documents.

practices.practice: Use multi-document transactions only when needed; keep transactions short, check preconditions early, and add retry logic to handle conflicts or transient failures.

practices.practice: Handle throttling (HTTP 429): detect 429 responses, respect the server-provided Retry-After header when present, and use exponential backoff with jitter rather than immediate retries.
practices.prior_belief: Handle rate limits and throttling (HTTP 429): detect 429 responses or explicit throttling errors, respect Retry‑After when provided, and perform exponential backoff with jitter rather than immediate retry loops.

practices.practice: Always page large result sets (use limit + sort + range filters or cursor.batchSize) and avoid unbounded server-side scans that stream huge result sets into application memory.
